harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent internal time synchronization. node1 serves cluster time over NTP, and node2 synchronizes exclusively from node1. Both nodes successfully restarted one at a time and recovered with changed boot identities, unchanged RHEL release/kernel, and healthy synchronization.
actions_performed: Used the installed RHEL-compatible chrony 4.8 package; no OS, kernel, or package upgrades were performed.
Configured node1 to use its upstream pool, permit 10.100.12.0/24, listen on UDP/123, and permanently allow NTP through firewalld.
Configured node2 with only `server 10.100.12.10 iburst prefer`; removed public and DHCP-provided time sources.
Enabled chronyd persistently and verified normal leap status and active synchronization.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially using native systemd reboot, verifying changed boot IDs and recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 operates as the internal time source
evidence.summary: Shows node1's allow rule, active/enabled chronyd, synchronized upstream source, UDP/123 listener, permanent firewall permission, and current NTP requests from node2.

evidence.requirement: node2 synchronizes against node1 instead of a public server
evidence.summary: Shows node2's sole configured source is 10.100.12.10 and that it selects node1 (^*) with NTPSynchronized=yes and normal leap status.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 before and after configuration and restarts.
Healthy baseline boot ID 6bb7e004…; acknowledged reboot; changed boot ID 4f0f2ad6…; recovered chronyd, listener, firewall and upstream synchronization; node2 then received fresh samples from node1.

Healthy baseline boot ID 437b338f…; acknowledged reboot; changed boot ID a58737ea…; recovered active/enabled chronyd and exclusive node1 synchronization; node1 directly recorded fresh requests from node2.

attempts.summary: Configured persistent internal time synchronization. node1 serves cluster time over NTP, and node2 synchronizes exclusively from node1. Both nodes successfully restarted one at a time and recovered with changed boot identities, unchanged RHEL release/kernel, and healthy synchronization.
